counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow applies a paired-samples t-test even though the task states the row pairing is a storage convention with no relationship between the items in a row. This is a serious misapplication (fabricated pairing yielding p=0.0039), but it is a different defect: no independent unit is entered into the procedure more than once, so it is outside the reviewed issue class and must not be recorded as it.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: st.ttest_rel applied despite task's no-pairing statement

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: All 12 rows carry pairwise-distinct k1 codes (u01–u12) and pairwise-distinct k2 codes, so no identified source item is entered more than once on either side.
evidence.observed_value: 12 distinct k1 and 12 distinct k2 codes over 12 rows (lines 2–13)

evidence.description: The applied procedure consumes each row exactly once (df=11 matches 12 difference scores), so no unit value is repeatedly entered.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict two ways: (a) duplicate scan of all k1 and k2 codes — every code appears exactly once, so no unit contributes multiple entries; (b) considering whether the ttest_rel misuse could be construed as this issue class — it cannot, because it involves an invented row-wise relationship, not repeated entry of any single authorized independent unit, and the scope instruction forbids recording other methodological concerns under this class. Both attempts failed to establish the in-scope issue.
